e-12467.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{2}+{y}^{-2}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2}) \\  & =4y-2{y}^{-3} \\  & =4y-\frac{2}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{4}-2}{{y}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy},$ we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm dx} = \left( \dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy} \right)^{-1} = \dfrac{y^3}{4y^4 -2}.
$$

e-12468.knowledge_point: Calculating dy/dx at a Point Using dx/dy
e-12468.problem: If $x = y + 2y\sqrt y$, find $\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm dx}$ at the point $\left(3 , 1\right).$
e-12468.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y+2y\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y+2{y}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2}) \\  & =1+2\cdot (\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}) \\  & =1+3{y}^{1/2} \\  & =1+3\sqrt{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy},$ we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm dx} = \left( \dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy} \right)^{-1} =  \dfrac{1}{1 + 3\sqrt y}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(3,1),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(3,1)} & =\frac{1}{1+3\sqrt{1}}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-12469.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
e-12469.problem: What is the equation of the tangent to the curve $x = 2y^2 -y + 1$ at the point $(2,1)?$
e-12469.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{2}-y+1) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(1) \\  & =2\cdot (2y)-1+0 \\  & =4y-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy},$ we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm dy}{\textrm dx} = \left( \dfrac{\textrm dx}{\textrm dy} \right)^{-1} = \dfrac1{4y - 1}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(2,1)$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(2,1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{4(1)-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{1}{3}(x-2) \\ y & =\frac{x}{3}-\frac{2}{3}+1 \\ y & =\frac{x}{3}+\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{2}{y}+\frac{8}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{-1}+8{y}^{-2}) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1})+8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-2}) \\  & =2\cdot (-{y}^{-2})+8\cdot (-2{y}^{-3}) \\  & =-2{y}^{-2}-16{y}^{-3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{{y}^{2}}-\frac{16}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{-2y-16}{{y}^{3}} \\  & =-\frac{2y+16}{{y}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=-\frac{{y}^{3}}{2y+16}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(3,2),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(3,2)} & =-\frac{{2}^{3}}{2(2)+16} \\  & =-\frac{8}{20} \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Given a curve $x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}-2{y}^{2},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-1,1)?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1/2})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{-3/2}-2\cdot (2y) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{y}^{3/2}}-4y \\  & =\frac{-1-8{y}^{5/2}}{2{y}^{3/2}} \\  & =-\frac{1+8{y}^{2}\sqrt{y}}{2y\sqrt{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=-\frac{2y\sqrt{y}}{1+8{y}^{2}\sqrt{y}}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-1,1)} \\  & =-\frac{2(1)\sqrt{1}}{1+8(1)^{2}\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{2}{9}(x-(-1)) \\ y & =-\frac{2}{9}x-\frac{2}{9}+1 \\ y & =-\frac{2}{9}x+\frac{7}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

Given a curve x=1y−2y2, what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point (−1,1)?

a
y=−92x−72
b
y=−29x+79
c
y=−29x−29
d
y=−92x+52
e
y=−29x+59
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we differentiate x(y) with respect to y:

dxdy=ddy(1y−2y2)=ddy(1y)−2ddy(y2)=ddy(y−1/2)−2ddy(y2)=−12y−3/2−2⋅(2y)=−12y3/2−4y=−1−8y5/22y3/2=−1+8y2y2yy.

Now, taking the reciprocal of dxdy, we get

dydx=(dxdy)−1=−2yy1+8y2y.

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point (−1,1) is m=dydx|(x,y)=(−1,1)=−2(1)11+8(1)21=−29.

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get y−y1=m(x−x1)y−1=−29(x−(−1))y=−29x−29+1y=−29x+79.

content.problem: Given a curve $x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}-2{y}^{2},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-1,1)?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-1/2})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{-3/2}-2\cdot (2y) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{y}^{3/2}}-4y \\  & =\frac{-1-8{y}^{5/2}}{2{y}^{3/2}} \\  & =-\frac{1+8{y}^{2}\sqrt{y}}{2y\sqrt{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=-\frac{2y\sqrt{y}}{1+8{y}^{2}\sqrt{y}}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(-1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(-1,1)} \\  & =-\frac{2(1)\sqrt{1}}{1+8(1)^{2}\sqrt{1}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{2}{9}(x-(-1)) \\ y & =-\frac{2}{9}x-\frac{2}{9}+1 \\ y & =-\frac{2}{9}x+\frac{7}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Given a curve $x=\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}-{y}^{2},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(9,3)?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot 3{y}^{2}-2y \\  & =2{y}^{2}-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2{y}^{2}-2y}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(9,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(9,3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2(3)^{2}-2(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =\frac{1}{12}(x-9) \\ y & =\frac{x}{12}-\frac{3}{4}+3 \\ y & =\frac{x}{12}+\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given a curve x=5y3−8y2+16, what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point (24,2)?

a
y=x28+17
b
y=x18−78
c
y=x28+167
d
y=x28+87
e
y=x8−87
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we differentiate x(y) with respect to y:

dxdy=ddy(5y3−8y2+16)=5ddy(y3)−8ddy(y2)+16ddy(1)=5⋅(3y2)−8⋅(2y)+0=15y2−16y.

Now, taking the reciprocal of dxdy, we get

dydx=(dxdy)−1=115y2−16y.

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point (24,2) is m=dydx|(x,y)=(24,2)=115⋅22−16⋅2=128.

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get y−y1=m(x−x1)y−2=128(x−24)y=x28−67+2y=x28+87.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the slope is 1/(15·2^2 − 16·2) = 1/28. The tangent through (24,2) is y − 2 = (x − 24)/28, hence y = x/28 + 8/7, option d.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Tangent Line Using dx/dy
content.problem: Given a curve $x=5{y}^{3}-8{y}^{2}+16,$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(24,2)?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(5{y}^{3}-8{y}^{2}+16) \\  & =5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3})-8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+16\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(1) \\  & =5\cdot (3{y}^{2})-8\cdot (2y)+0 \\  & =15{y}^{2}-16y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{15{y}^{2}-16y}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(24,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(24,2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{15\cdot {2}^{2}-16\cdot 2} \\  & =\frac{1}{28}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =\frac{1}{28}(x-24) \\ y & =\frac{x}{28}-\frac{6}{7}+2 \\ y & =\frac{x}{28}+\frac{8}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
